verdict.rationale: cubic.yaml and 'custom agents' let a team encode natural-language review rules that are enforced across PRs (cubic-docs-9, cubic-docs-11), and cubic learns from human feedback to calibrate what's useful (cubic-docs-10). However there is no evidence of AST-pattern rule definition or linking external style guides, and a community reviewer explicitly flags that a YAML/plain-text rule approach is a 'half-measure' compared to code-native architectural tests (cubic-comm-2). Missing for 10: documented AST pattern matching, support for linking/importing external style guide documents, and independent confirmation that custom agents reliably enforce complex rules.
